items.why: The report fits the doublet with two Lorentzians: "broad band at 351.09 cm-1 ... assigned 2LA(M); narrow band at 355.28 cm-1 ... assigned E2g1", and says "The two-peak fit matters".
It gives "2LA(M)/A1g height ratio: about 2.2 at spot 1 ... and about 0.47 at spot 2" and cites the ~2 monolayer value at 514 nm.
It reports "A1g moves up +2.8 cm-1 (417.3 to 420.1)" and reads this as 1L at spot 1 and 3L/bulk-like at spot 2.
It gives "62.0 cm-1 at spot 1 ... and 64.7 cm-1 at spot 2" from the two-component fit, and notes that single-peak fits give a biased 65.6 and 67.0.

It says "the same data cannot separate 3L from bulk" (64.6 vs 64.8), notes the 1L–2L difference is "only 1.4 cm-1", and lists A1g steps 418.4, 419.0, 420.1, so it shows that layer number beyond 1L is weakly constrained.

It calibrates against the Si line ("Si line 520.91 cm-1 (offset +0.21 from 520.7)", "--si-correct"), warns that the result rests on "one laser wavelength", and cites the dependence of 2LA(M) on resonance.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly rejects the blended single-peak maximum: "Their derived separations of 65.6 and 67.0 cm-1 are biased and should not be used for layer number."
It assigns 2LA(M) as a second-order mode and says the 176 cm-1 band "is not a defect marker"; it never calls 2LA(M) a defect peak.
